div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
one leg = one direction of one call (D26).
Speaker identity is STRUCTURAL — no diarisation
model to be wrong about who spoke

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
open_leg is IDEMPOTENT since D110, and it is a
CORRECTNESS fix. Two consumers now open a leg and
neither may depend on the other running (D12).
Replacing it would discard the first one's sinks —
correct, running, fed nothing, which is B24.
On a format disagreement the FIRST wins and the
second is logged: silently decoding A-law as u-law
is loud plausible garbage nobody blames on the codec

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
services/transcription — subscriber #1
endpoints, transcribes, publishes turns

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
frames appended per leg, in memory.
Capped at MAX_SAMPLES (600 s): a stuck media source
keeps recording and stops accumulating, and says so —
the same shape as B20's backlog cap

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
close(session) — CHEAP, and it runs INSIDE the accept.
It moves a list onto a queue and returns. An object-store
round trip between the agent pressing Accept and the caller
hearing them is D12's rule broken in a new place.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CONSENT IS CHECKED HERE, at the last possible moment.
The offer window IS the recording window (D21), so a caller
who pressed 2 has had frames flowing the whole time and no
recording consent. Their speech is transcribed IN MEMORY for
the brief and stored NOWHERE. Checking at open() would be too
early: consent arrives on a keypress that can land after the leg.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
call.state.changed -> TERMINAL: seal too.
Nobody presses Accept for a caller who hangs up while
waiting, so without this their buffer sits open for the
life of the process. WRAP_UP is not terminal (D106)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
flush_pending() — from sweep_once, never from a request (B7).
A failed upload KEEPS ITS PLACE and retries next pass.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
EncryptingBlobStorage wraps ANY backend.
Four implementations exist and more will; four copies of
the cryptography means one nobody reviewed is the one
holding a real recording.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ports/keyring.py — the TENTH port.
LocalKeyRing: master from RECORDING_MASTER_KEY.
Unset = generated per process + a warning, which is
coherent ONLY with BLOB_STORAGE=memory. Any durable
store REFUSES TO START without one: ciphertext nobody
can ever read is worse than an honest gap.
P7 swaps this for a vault; nothing else changes.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
RCE1 | key_ref | wrapped data key | nonce | AES-256-GCM
Self-describing: restoring one recording needs the
ring and that object, and nothing else.
A blob without RCE1 is returned untouched — which is
how plaintext prompt clips keep working.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
memory / localfs / s3 (MinIO is s3 with an endpoint).
localfs is ALLOWED NOW: the old refusal protected a property
the wrapper now guarantees by construction. build_blob_storage
is the enforcement point — nothing in services/ builds one.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
audio_recordings — the INDEX, never the audio and never the key.
storage_ref, encryption_key_ref (the MASTER, not the data key),
checksum OF THE PLAINTEXT (GCM's nonce is fresh every write, so
a checksum of the ciphertext could never answer 'same recording?'),
and delete_after.
WRITTEN ONLY AFTER THE STORE CONFIRMS: a reference to an object
that was never written is a recording that looks retrievable,
satisfies an audit, and plays nothing.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
delete_after is stamped AT UPLOAD TIME from
RECORDING_RETENTION_DAYS (D14) — not computed at purge time.
Otherwise lowering the setting silently shortens the life of
audio already held, and the promise that matters is the one
made when the caller said yes.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
scripts/purge_recordings.py — D14's erasure job.
A SCRIPT, not a background task: deletion is the thing you
least want happening unattended on a demo machine.
THE OBJECT GOES BEFORE THE ROW — the other order leaves audio
nobody knows they hold, invisible to every report.
Refuses on STORAGE_BACKEND=memory, where a clean run would be
a green tick over an untouched bucket.
